name: Templo de Diana (Mérida)

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/202213495 (centroid of the podium; long axis at 143.1°, the front with the base of the stair to the south-east)

rights.note: Roman temple of the imperial cult, time of Tiberius (14–37 AD), architect unknown; the palace of the Conde de los Corbos inside it is of the 16th century. Monumento nacional 1912, UNESCO World Heritage (Archaeological Ensemble of Mérida) 1993.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q18808444_templo_de_diana_merida.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. Granite podium 3.23 m with moulded base and cornice, ashlar in courses and rubble where the facing is lost. Corinthian columns of 8 m (Attic base, fluted shaft in drums, acanthus capital) on the 3.18 × 3.02 m grid of a hexastyle peripteros with 11 columns per flank. Standing: the six front columns with their architrave, the rebuilt attic and relieving arch; a second row one bay behind (pronaos) joined to the front by beams; the south-west flank with nine columns (architrave over the first seven); the north-east flank with three free columns at the front, three half-sunk in the palace wall and one at the palace's rear corner; stumps and loose drums on the rear of the podium. The palace of the Conde de los Corbos (16th c.) in the cella: two floors, cream render, a two-storey Renaissance loggia on the front, arched windows on the south-west side, two Mudéjar twin windows in brick frames and two arched doors on the north-east side, hipped tile roof. Around: the sandy precinct with a granite band round the podium, the two Roman pools (dry, excavated, with railings) and the excavation of the stair in front with its steel walkway. Uncertain: exactly which flank columns survive at the rear (from photos), the inner pronaos columns, the palace windows and roof height (±1 m), the depth of the pools and of the excavation.
